title: chenopodium album subsp. ambrosioides
intro: Chenopodium album subsp. ambrosioides, commonly known as Mexican tea or epazote, is a plant species native to the Americas and part of the Amaranthaceae family. It has been used for its medicinal properties, including reducing flatulence and alleviating digestive issues, making it beneficial for overall health. The therapeutic actions of Mexican tea include its ability to act as an antispasmodic, anti-inflammatory, and expectorant, helping to relieve respiratory issues and soothe the digestive system. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, terpenoids, and essential oils, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
